title: Peek doesnt work when idle for a while

judgment.rationale: The multi-file symptom and tray-based recovery point to a Peek lifecycle boundary, and the owning code is identifiable, but the idle failure state is not logged.
evidence: Space activation fails after idle and recovers after opening PowerToys.
CSV, text, and Markdown are affected.
Current Peek code owns viewer process state and hotkey activation.
judgment.recommended_action: Request the failure-time lifecycle trace and approve the stale-state recovery design.

fix_assessment.rationale: The Peek hotkey path keeps process state across the viewer lifecycle; a stale handle/PID or a failed relaunch can make Space appear inert until another PowerToys UI action recovers the process.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover Peek viewer state after idle or failed launch
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Peek hotkey path keeps process state across the viewer lifecycle; a stale handle/PID or a failed relaunch can make Space appear inert until another PowerToys UI action recovers the process.
plan: Make viewer launch success explicit and store handles/PIDs only after successful launch.
Clear stale process state when the viewer exits or cannot be queried.
Relaunch and signal the invoke event only after a valid viewer is confirmed.
verification: Test CSV, text, and Markdown activation after idle.
Test viewer exit, one failed launch, sleep/resume, and repeated Space presses without duplicate viewers.

confidence.rationale: The reported recovery after opening the tray UI fits a stale viewer lifecycle, but no log confirms whether the idle failure is launch, exit detection, or event signaling.

issue_context.summary: Peek stops responding to Space after being idle, then works again after opening PowerToys from the taskbar; the issue affects multiple text-like file types.
known_information: PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store is reported.
The failure recovers after opening the PowerToys UI.
CSV, text, and Markdown are named as affected file types.
Current Peek code owns viewer process state, launch, enable/disable, and hotkey activation.
inferences: The idle interval may allow the viewer to exit or leave stale process state.
Opening the tray UI may trigger lifecycle refresh rather than fix the file handlers.
issue_context.analysis: The process-lifecycle path is a reasonable yellow design target, but a failure-time trace should distinguish stale process state from hotkey registration or file association issues.
initial_investigation: dllmain.cpp contains is_viewer_running, launch_process, enable/disable, and on_hotkey.
The report has no bug report or timing interval, so exact lifecycle state is not observable.
No stronger duplicate was identified from the current public issue search.

information_gaps.information: The idle duration and Peek viewer/hotkey state at the first failed Space activation.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes viewer exit/stale state from registration or file-association failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce after a measured idle interval and submit `/bugreport` immediately after the first failed activation, before opening the tray UI.

actions.label: Request Peek idle-state trace
actions.note: Ask for the timing and lifecycle evidence needed to choose the fix branch.

comment.body: The report already narrows the symptom to Peek: Space does nothing for CSV/text/Markdown after being idle, then works after opening PowerToys. Please reproduce once after noting the approximate idle time, and submit `/bugreport` immediately after the first failed Space activation before opening the tray UI. This will show whether the Peek viewer exited, whether the hotkey is still registered, and whether the recovery action merely refreshes stale process state.

actions.label: Design fix: recover Peek viewer lifecycle
actions.note: Approve a fork-side lifecycle investigation and stale-state fix if the trace confirms the viewer path.
actions.design_prompt: Trace Peek viewer launch/state/hotkey recovery after idle, then harden stale process cleanup and relaunch signaling without duplicating viewers.

design.root_cause: The Peek hotkey path keeps process state across the viewer lifecycle; a stale handle/PID or a failed relaunch can make Space appear inert until another PowerToys UI action recovers the process.
evidence: Peek dllmain.cpp owns is_viewer_running, launch_process, and on_hotkey.
The symptom is recovered by opening the PowerToys UI, suggesting a lifecycle refresh.
The report affects several file types, making a single file parser less likely.

affected_files.purpose: Owns Peek enablement, viewer process lifecycle, and global hotkey activation.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Process state can outlive a failed launch or an exited viewer.
implementation_steps.change: Return launch success, assign process state only on success, and clear stale handles/PIDs when querying the viewer.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (!launch_process()) { clear_viewer_state(); return false; } viewer_state = ValidProcess(handle, pid);
edge_cases: Avoid treating an exited process as running.
tests: Test failed launch and exited viewer recovery.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Hotkey activation may signal stale state instead of relaunching a valid viewer.
implementation_steps.change: Clean state first, then relaunch or signal only a confirmed running viewer.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (!is_viewer_running()) { clear_viewer_state(); if (!launch_process()) return false; } signal_invoke_event();
tests: Test repeated Space activation after idle and sleep/resume.

verify: Build Peek and its viewer components.
Reproduce CSV/text/Markdown activation after idle without opening Settings/tray first.
Test viewer exit, launch failure, sleep/resume, and repeated activation.
risks: Viewer lifecycle timing may differ between Store and desktop installs.
Aggressive cleanup could race a viewer that is still starting.
alternatives: Changing file handlers is lower confidence because multiple file types fail and the tray action recovers the behavior.
Blindly relaunching on every hotkey is rejected because it can create duplicate viewers.
